title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
abstract: arXiv:2605.30329v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Autonomous AI research agents aim to speed up scientific discovery by automating the research pipeline from hypothesis generation to peer review. However, existing benchmarks rarely test a fundamental bottleneck whether LLMs can judge the methodological viability of a research idea $\textbf{before}$ investing time and computational resources. Without a reliable ``first-gate'' filter, autonomous agents risk scaling flawed methodology rather than accelerating meaningful science. We introduce $\textbf{SoundnessBench}$, a curated benchmark of 1,099 real research proposals, with source verified extraction, reviewer-derived proxy labels, and proposal-only expert judgments on a subset of 327 proposals. Across 12 frontier LLMs, our evaluation reveals a pervasive $\textbf{optimism bias}$: standard prompting yields a $74.0\%$ mean false-positive rate. Aggressive prompting reduces false approvals but substantially increases false rejections. Ad

translated_title: SoundnessBench：你的AI科学家真的能分辨好研究想法与坏研究想法吗？
translated_abstract: 自主AI研究智能体旨在通过自动化从假设生成到同行评审的整个研究流程来加速科学发现。然而，现有基准很少测试一个根本性的瓶颈：大语言模型能否在投入时间和计算资源**之前**判断一个研究想法的方法论可行性。如果没有可靠的“第一道关卡”过滤器，自主智能体可能会规模化推广有缺陷的方法论，而非加速有意义的科学进展。我们提出了SoundnessBench，这是一个精心构建的基准，包含1,099个真实研究提案，具有来源验证的提取方式、来自评审员的代理标签，以及对其中327个提案子集的仅基于提案内容的专家判断。通过对12个前沿大语言模型的评估，我们揭示了一种普遍存在的**乐观偏见**：在标准提示下，平均假阳性率高达74.0%。采用激进提示可以减少错误批准，但会显著增加错误拒绝。
tldr: 提出了包含1,099个真实研究提案的SoundnessBench基准，评估发现12个前沿大语言模型普遍存在乐观偏见（平均假阳性率74.0%），无法可靠地在投入资源前甄别研究想法的方法论缺陷。
en_tdlr: SoundnessBench, a curated benchmark of 1,099 real research proposals, reveals that 12 frontier LLMs exhibit a pervasive optimism bias with a 74.0% mean false-positive rate, failing to reliably judge the methodological viability of research ideas before resources are invested.
